We've not made a figure since Monday, which is a bad look for a data science class!

Don't worry, we did that deliberately. For two full days we've been exploring the TableLands: grouped, aggregated,
joined, stacked, pivoted and parsed. Some of those tables held real findings, and you could read them off the way you read a spreadsheet, one number at a time. 

Today we take our last step, and it is the one all the others have been prepping us for. You will learn the anatomy of a
figure in python, so that you can control how it looks instead of accepting whatever the defaults give you. Then you
will work with a plotting library that takes a whole table and the names of two columns and does the rest. 

Finally, this afternoon, you will pick your project.

what you can say about the differences between them.
